writeup.headline: NVIDIA rates Buy on exceptional growth and margins, held back by middling valuation, trend and news scores.
writeup.thesis: NVIDIA scores 77, a Buy, 3 points short of Strong Buy. Growth scores 100, with TTM revenue growth of 83.4% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 105.8% year on year, and growth sped up by 20.6 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (97) and balance sheet (98) are near the top: a 65.2% operating margin, a 41.9% FCF margin, diluted share count down 1.0% year on year and a net cash position. Valuation scores only 54 because the multiples are high in absolute terms (17.3x sales, 41.4x FCF, FCF yield 2.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), though the stock is cheap against its own history, with EV/EBIT cheaper than at every one of the last 61 month-ends. A middling trend score of 58 (shares 8.1 pp behind QQQ over the last 126 trading days) and a news score of 54 keep the total below the top band.
key_risks: Absolute valuation is high at 17.3x sales and 41.4x FCF, which leaves little room if growth slows.
Early-stage DOJ antitrust inquiry into the Hugging Face acquisition, reportedly extending to other deals.
Competition from Google TPUs, including a report that OpenAI plans to buy them.
Weak relative price trend: shares 6.6 pp behind SPY and 1.9% below the 50-day average.
Q3 FY27 guidance of $108.0 billion assumes no China Data Center compute revenue, so export policy remains a swing factor.
what_would_change: A 3-point gain, for example from a stronger trend score or positive news after the Nov 17 report, would lift the rating to Strong Buy.
A 13-point drop would push the rating to Hold. This would likely need a growth slowdown together with weaker trend or news scores.
An escalating DOJ inquiry or a guidance cut would pull the news risk score down.
Further multiple expansion would weigh on the valuation score.
